newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ryanair says to cease cargo operation.
newsitem.headline: Ryanair says to cease cargo operation.

text.p: Irish independent, low-cost, no-frills airline Ryanair said on Tuesday it planned to cease carrying cargo with effect from September 14.
The group said in a statement its decision came as a result of the termination of a contract with its cargo sales agent, PACE Airlines Services Ltd.
It said the move was also aimed at improving both the cost and efficiency of its passenger services.
The loss of cargo income would have insignificant impact on revenues, representing less that half a percentage point of total turnover, Ryanair said.
"In order to further improve our on-time performance, we have had to review all aspects of our operation," commercial director Tim Jeans said.
He said Ryanair had concluded that without substantially increasing its cargo rates, the returns from cargo did not justify the operational impact it had on turnaround deadlines.

Jeans estimated Ryanair's standard turnaround time currently at 25 minutes. "...we therefore believe that we can further improve our on-time departures and customer service by dispensing with our cargo," he said.
